To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

BMIM( +) cations have strong tendency to accumulate around protein surface whereas Cl( -) anions are repelled from protein surface; and the accumulation of large BMIM(+) on protein surface could stabilize the backbone hydrogen bonding and thus protein structure.

BMIM( + ) cations accumulate on protein surface and have both electrostatic and hydrophobic interactions, which could remove the surrounding waters and stabilize the backbone hydrogen bonding, thus stabilizing protein structure.

BMIM(±) cations accumulate on protein surface and stabilize the protein structure by electrostatic and hydrophobic interactions, and also by reducing the hydrogen bonding from the surrounding water to protein.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of water-miscibility ionic liquid (BMIM-CL) on the structure of the α-helix bundle protein (the B domain from staphylococcal protein A).
the effect of ionic liquids on protein structure stability.
the molecular mechanism of ionic liquid on the stability of protein.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
BMIM(++) cations could stabilize protein structure via electrostatic and hydrophobic interactions and by expelling the surrounding water molecules.

the protein stability in the ionic liquid solution is a result of the balance of the electrostatic interactions, hydrophobic interactions, and the water structure around the protein, which are all affected by the properties of the ionic liquid.
BMIM-Cl ionic liquid has a positive effect on protein stability.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the protein structure is stabilized by the electrostatic and hydrophobic interaction between the ionic liquid cation and the protein, the reduction of water molecules around the protein, and the increase of backbone hydrogen bonds.
the accumulation of ionic liquids on protein surface is a key factor for the protein stabilization.
BMIM-Cl could stabilize the native structure of protein by electrostatic interactions, hydrophobic interactions, and the removal of water molecules from the protein surface.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the protein structure stability is enhanced when the protein is dissolved in ionic liquids, which is consistent with experimental observations.
the accumulation of large size BMIM(+) on the protein surface could reduce the hydrogen bond between protein and solvent and stabilize the protein backbone.

the protein stabilization in BMIM-CL solutions is mainly attributed to the hydrophobic interactions between protein and BMIM(+) ions, the hydrogen bonding between BMIM(+) and protein, as well as the dehydration of protein surface by BMIM(+) accumulation.
